title: Sharp logarithmic exponents for fixed off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
main_claim: For every fixed s>=6: t^{s-1}/(log t)^{s-2+eps} <= r(s,t) <= C_s t^{s-1}/(log t)^{s-2}. The lower bound comes from a random ordered incident-flag graph on floor(q^d log q) vertices in PG(d,q), d=s-1. It is K_{d+1}-free, and alpha < q(log q)^{1+eta} by an entropy-compression contradiction.
coverage:
Checked in detail:
- Foundations: incidence variance identity, K_{d+1}-freeness, simultaneous rectangle occupancy, and the selected-tuple entropy bound. I recomputed log(eN/l)=(d-1)sigma-eta log sigma+O(1).
- New repeated-projection reduction for j>=4: center properties, collision bound E coll<=C|A|^2/q^{j-1}, the Cauchy-Schwarz contraction rho<=q^{-1/4+o(1)} with |A_8|=O(m_0), per-call loss <.02n, and how the gap parameters change.
- Fresh validation lemma.
- Marking scan for general d: the O(q sigma) expensive count via the U_l shrinkage, popular- and poor-cheap domain bounds, the split into reciprocal and high classes (r+r'<=d+1 vs >d+1), and the core-dimension band arguments for open and integer bands, including the containment U_j(y) in V_i(a)^perp and the rectangle charging.
- Representative exposure (total-correlation telescoping) and the good-index proportions.
- New rich-subspace union lemma: Schwartz-Zippel vanishing on rich subspaces, and the box-partition lower bound on evaluation rank. Correct.
- New high-rank two-row description: coverage via consistency plus KL event transfer (o(1) conflict over 2h samples), the excess-dimension span bound Ce^K/q, and the size bound via the rich union plus a dyadic binomial tail that sums geometrically.
- Reciprocal tree: product bound, the u-ordering deletion count, potential recursion and cost.
- Iteration recurrence D_new<=sigma^{2beta}+D sigma^{-eta/4}, final budgets, prime interval, the t-conversion exponent d-1+d eta, and the AKS-style upper bound.
Not re-derived line by line: the low-dimensional (j=2,3) learning moments and rich-line polynomial lemma. These are shared with the r(5,t) companion, which sibling rank 239 checked.
sibling_notes: Companion of The-Sharp-Logarithmic-Exponent-of-r-5-t (rank 239, no_gap_found). It shares the marking, learning and low-dimensional geometry essentially verbatim. What is new here: the projection induction for dimension j>=4, the rich-subspace union lemma, and the high-rank (r+r'>d+1) two-row description. All three check out.
